hindi: प्रत्येक धनात्मक पूर्णांक $n$ के लिए, माना कि $S_{n}=\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4k}{k^{4}-k^{2}+4}\right)$ है, जहाँ $\tan^{-1}$ के मान $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ में हैं। तब $S_{2}+S_{3}$ बराबर है
solution_full: For $a,b\ge0$ we have $ab>-1$, so the subtraction formula $\tan^{-1}a-\tan^{-1}b=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{a-b}{1+ab}$ holds without correction. Therefore $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{4k}{k^{4}-k^{2}+4}\right)=\tan^{-1}T_{k}-\tan^{-1}T_{k-1}$.

Adding for $k=1,2,\ldots,n$, the sum telescopes: $S_{n}=\tan^{-1}T_{n}-\tan^{-1}T_{0}=\tan^{-1}\dfrac{n(n+1)}{2}$. Check: $S_{1}=\tan^{-1}1=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, and the first term is $\tan^{-1}\dfrac{4}{4}=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

For the addition, both numbers are positive and $3\cdot6=18>1$, so $\tan^{-1}3+\tan^{-1}6>\dfrac{\pi}{2}$ and the addition formula needs the correction $\pi$: $\tan^{-1}3+\tan^{-1}6=\pi+\tan^{-1}\dfrac{3+6}{1-18}=\pi+\tan^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{9}{17}\right)=\pi-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{9}{17}$.
(Forgetting the correction gives the negative value $-\tan^{-1}\dfrac{9}{17}$, impossible for a sum of positive angles.)
originality_note: New: the general term 4k/(k^4-k^2+4) is decoded as a difference of arctangents of consecutive triangular numbers, and the finite partial sums tan^-1 3 + tan^-1 6 are then added, which needs the pi-correction (way 5). Closest known: telescoping sums of tan^-1(1/(n^2+n+1)) and the published identity sum tan^-1(2ak/(k^4-k^2+a^2)) = pi/2. Different because: the question asks for a sum of two partial sums, not the infinite series, so the addition formula with its branch correction carries the answer.

concept_use.Summation of series based on ITF: The series is telescoped with u_k = k(k+1)/2 to get S_n = tan^-1(n(n+1)/2).
concept_use.Addition and subtractions of angles invo: Each term is written as tan^-1 T_k - tan^-1 T_(k-1), and S_2 + S_3 = tan^-1 3 + tan^-1 6 needs the xy > 1 case with +pi.
